title: Universal property of algebra base change
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, let $A$ be a commutative $R$-algebra, and let $B$ be a commutative $S$-algebra, regarded as an $R$-algebra through $R\to S\to B$. Then restriction along $a\mapsto 1\otimes a$ gives a bijection between $S$-algebra homomorphisms $S\otimes_R A\to B$ and $R$-algebra homomorphisms $A\to B$. Its inverse sends $f:A\to B$ to the unique $S$-algebra homomorphism with $(s\otimes a)\mapsto s\,f(a)$.

source.place: Algebra, Section 00CV (tensor products of algebras); the displayed universal property is the standard coproduct/base-change property, and is realized in Mathlib by AlgHom.liftEquiv
